title: Greedy choices
description:
```cpp
int maxMeetings(std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> meetings);          // (start, end); end > start; one room
int roomsNeeded(const std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>& meetings);   // rooms to hold them all
long long huffmanBits(const std::vector<long long>& frequencies);    // total bits of an optimal prefix code
double fractionalKnapsack(std::vector<std::pair<double, double>> items, double capacity);   // (weight, value)
```

- A meeting `(s, e)` occupies the half-open time `[s, e)`: one ending at 5 does not overlap one starting at 5.
- `huffmanBits` repeatedly merges the two smallest weights with a min-heap and adds up the merged weights. With fewer than two symbols the answer is 0 (a single symbol needs no bits to tell it apart). Frequencies of 0 still take part.
- `fractionalKnapsack`: take items by value per unit of weight, best first, taking a fraction of the last one. Items with weight 0 are always taken whole.
- The tests use 100,000 meetings, so these must be O(n log n).
hints: For `roomsNeeded`, turn each meeting into two events, `(start, +1)` and `(end, -1)`, and sort them. Pairs sort by time and then by the second value, so at equal times the `-1` comes first: a room freed at 5 is reused by a meeting starting at 5.
`std::priority_queue` can be built straight from a range: `std::priority_queue<long long, std::vector<long long>, std::greater<long long>> heap(v.begin(), v.end());` heapifies in O(n).
